config.title: resize and overflow

intro.title: resize and overflow
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive webpage that demonstrates how to control the size and content display of HTML elements. You will learn the core CSS concepts of the 'resize' property, which allows users to adjust an element's dimensions, and the 'overflow' property, which manages content that exceeds an element's boundaries. The main technologies involved are CSS properties applied to HTML div elements. By the end, you'll understand how to make elements resizable and handle overflowing content effectively.
intro.usecase: The resize and overflow properties are essential for creating flexible, user-friendly interfaces where content dimensions vary. In dashboards and analytics tools, resize allows users to adjust data panels and charts to their preferred viewing size, while overflow handles scrollable tables and lists that contain more data than fits in the allocated space. Text editors and code editors use overflow to manage scrollable content areas, and resize for adjustable sidebars or panels. These properties are also crucial in admin panels where filter sections need to be resizable and content containers must gracefully handle overflow without breaking the layout.

objectives: Apply the resize property to enable user-adjustable dimensions on HTML elements.
Configure overflow behavior to control content visibility outside an element's boundaries.
Manipulate overflow-x and overflow-y properties to handle horizontal and vertical scrolling independently.
Integrate resize and overflow properties to create interactive, scrollable content areas.
Construct a UI component that combines resizable containers with managed content overflow.
Control scrollbar appearance and behavior using overflow values like auto, scroll, and hidden.
Implement a practical layout where resizable elements maintain proper overflow handling.

steps.title: Create a container element with fixed dimensions
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a class named 'container' that sets its width to 400px and height to 300px.
steps.hint: Use the .container selector and define width and height properties with pixel values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule that defines a container with fixed dimensions of 400px by 300px.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a .container selector with width: 400px; and height: 300px; properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both width and height are set to the specified pixel values.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using the correct class name (.container) and setting both width and height properties with px units.

steps.title: Create a resizable element with the resize property
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a class named 'resizable-box' that sets resize: both to allow user resizing in both directions.
steps.hint: The resize property controls whether an element can be resized by the user. Use 'both' to allow resizing horizontally and vertically.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule .resizable-box with resize: both will be created, allowing the element to be resized by the user.
successCriteria: The .resizable-box rule exists and includes resize: both.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the .resizable-box rule, but it's missing the resize: both property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .resizable-box rule with resize: both wasn't found. Make sure to add the rule with the correct property.

steps.title: Limit resize direction to horizontal only
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the .resizable-box class that sets the resize property to 'horizontal' to allow only width resizing.
steps.hint: Use the resize property with the value 'horizontal' to restrict resizing to the horizontal direction only.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .resizable-box element will only be resizable horizontally (width can be changed, height remains fixed).
successCriteria: The .resizable-box rule includes the property resize: horizontal.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the resize property with the value 'horizontal' to the .resizable-box rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .resizable-box rule should include resize: horizontal to limit resizing to the horizontal direction.

steps.title: Limit resize direction to vertical only
steps.instruction: In the .resizable-box rule, set the resize property to 'vertical' to allow only height resizing.
steps.hint: Use the CSS property resize with the value 'vertical' to restrict resizing to the vertical direction only.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .resizable-box element will now only be resizable vertically (height can be changed, width remains fixed).
successCriteria: The .resizable-box rule contains the property resize: vertical.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the exact property 'resize: vertical' in the .resizable-box rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the resize property with value 'vertical' to the .resizable-box rule.

steps.title: Combine resize and overflow properties
steps.instruction: Update the .resizable-box rule to include both resize: both and overflow: auto properties.
steps.hint: Add both properties to the same CSS rule to make the element resizable in all directions with automatic scrollbars when content overflows.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .resizable-box element will become fully interactive - users can resize it horizontally and vertically, and scrollbars will automatically appear when content exceeds the container size.
successCriteria: The .resizable-box rule contains both 'resize: both' and 'overflow: auto' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both 'resize: both' and 'overflow: auto' to the .resizable-box rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .resizable-box rule needs to be updated. Add both 'resize: both' and 'overflow: auto' properties to create an interactive, scrollable container.
